html:
Rohtas Fort is a vast fortress near Jhelum in northern Punjab, Pakistan, begun in 1541 by Sher Shah Suri, the Afghan ruler of North India.

Sher Shah had just driven the Mughal emperor Humayun out of India. He built Rohtas to block Humayun's return through the northwest and to hold down the Gakhar tribes, who backed the Mughals. Its stone walls run for about four kilometres, with 68 towers and 12 gates, in a style that mixes Afghan and Persian ideas.

The fort was hardly ever tested. Sher Shah died in 1545, and Humayun came back ten years later, with the garrison giving up without a fight. Later Mughals used it only as a stop on the road. Little changed since, it has been a World Heritage Site since 1997, and the dynasty's other lasting work was the silver rupee.
sum: Rohtas Fort is a vast fortress near Jhelum in northern Punjab, Pakistan, begun in 1541 by Sher Shah Suri, the Afghan ruler of North India.
